title: The Hunter and La Silla
caption: Orion, the Pleiades and airglow over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This long-exposure photograph takes in the busy site of ESO's La Silla Observatory, the far-off glow of roads and towns in Chile's Atacama Desert, and a faint green airglow, light produced in Earth's upper atmosphere.

Low over the mountains, the source points to the Pleiades open star cluster, known in myth as the Seven Sisters. Directly above them is the constellation Orion, the Hunter. Red patches around the figure of the hunter are huge clouds and arcs of ionised gas, known as emission nebulae, and the Milky Way cuts its way across the sky.

The picture was taken by ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek. It brings together the observatory, the lights of the wider region, the glow of the atmosphere and the stars in one frame. Emission nebulae glow because gas in them is ionised by energetic starlight.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure night landscape photograph by Petr Horálek. The source gives no other camera or colour details.
understand.eye: The long exposure collects far more light than the eye, so faint features such as the green airglow and red nebulae show far more strongly than they would to an observer.

alt: An observatory on a mountain at night with distant glowing lights, a faint green glow in the sky, a star cluster low over the peaks and a constellation with red patches of gas above it.
